messages.subject: support for legacy markdown formats?
parts:
Hi list,

I have a bunch of older knitr files that still use the html-comment style syntax 

<!--begin.rcode chunckname
1+1
end.rcode-->

saved as filename_knit_.md files.  Is there anything I can toggle in knitr 0.8 so I can knit these files without needing to install some legacy version of knitr?

Many thanks.  

-Carl

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] support for legacy markdown formats?
parts:
The input syntax is orthogonal to the output, e.g. you can use the
HTML syntax for Markdown, but render Markdown output as well. To
override the default syntax, you can use pat_html().

library(knitr)
pat_html()
render_markdown()

knit(text = '
<!--begin.rcode chunckname
1+1
end.rcode-->
')

I guess it should be easy to convert the legacy markdown syntax to the
current syntax, e.g. (not tested)

for (f in list.files(pattern = '_knit_\\.md$')) {
txt = readLines(f)
txt = gsub('^<!--begin.rcode(.*)', '```{r \\1}', txt)
txt = gsub('\\s*end.rcode-->', '```', txt)
writeLines(txt, f)
}

Regards,
Yihui
